proof.text: Fix $x^\prime\in T^\prime$ and any charts $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $W=\operatorname{Spec}C$ as in the statement. The inclusions $u(V)\subset U$ and $W\subset g^{-1}(U)$ give the restricted maps $V\to U$ and $W\to U$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] with $(X,Y,S)=(T,S^\prime,S)$: the canonical map $V\times_UW\to T^\prime$ identifies its source, compatibly with both projections, with the open subscheme $V^\prime=p^{-1}(V)\cap q^{-1}(W)$. Since $p(x^\prime)\in V$ and $q(x^\prime)\in W$, this open contains $x^\prime$. In Lean, take m = pullback.map and use Scheme.pullback_map_isOpenImmersion and Scheme.Pullback.range_map. The open inclusion and m have equal ranges, so IsOpenImmersion.isoOfRangeEq gives the isomorphism, and isoOfRangeEq_hom_fac gives its compatibility with the ambient pullback.

Give $B,C$ the $A$-algebra structures from $V\to U$, $W\to U$: by [def-weil-affine-spectrum] each of these morphisms of affine spectra is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of exactly one ring homomorphism, $A\to B$, respectively $A\to C$. Write $i:V\times_UW\xrightarrow{\sim}V^\prime$ for step 1. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] with $(R,A,B)=(A,B,C)$ to obtain $j:V\times_UW\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A C)$. Then $j\circ i^{-1}$ is the asserted affine presentation. The projection formulas of that node identify the maps to $V,W$ with the spectra of $b\mapsto b\otimes1$ and $c\mapsto1\otimes c$. If $r_V,r_W$ are the projections from $V\times_UW$ and $e_V:V\hookrightarrow T$, $e_W:W\hookrightarrow S^\prime$ are the inclusions, step 1 gives $p|_{V^\prime}\circ i=e_V\circ r_V$ and $q|_{V^\prime}\circ i=e_W\circ r_W$. Composing with $i^{-1}$ identifies both restricted projections under $j\circ i^{-1}$ with the stated tensor maps, followed by $e_V,e_W$. Canonicity is relative to the fixed chart presentations and their structure maps: any two resulting identifications, composed with $j^{-1}$, have the same two projections to $V,W$, hence agree by uniqueness in [def-pc-fibre-product]. The equations are pullbackSpecIso_hom_fst and pullbackSpecIso_hom_snd. Cancel the open immersions iV and iW and apply pullback.hom_ext and Iso.ext to prove uniqueness.

The base-change clause of [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability] applies to the ind-etale map $A\to B$ of the chosen chart and the arbitrary map $A\to C$. Its base-changed map has source $C$ and target $B\otimes_A C$, with structure homomorphism $c\mapsto1\otimes c$; hence this homomorphism is ind-etale. By the second projection formula established in step 2, it is precisely the coordinate map of $V^\prime\to W$. Thus the ind-etale conclusion is for the projection $q$, with no restriction on $A\to C$. Use the already-proved source-library RingHom.IndEtale.isStableUnderBaseChange clause directly, with the right algebra structure on B tensor_A C; the other clauses of the bundled Sheaf stability theorem are not needed. Transport IndEtaleAcrossUniverses to and from the equal-universe predicate along the canonical ULift ring equivalences, using invariance under ring isomorphisms.

For any $x^\prime\in T^\prime$, choose $V,U$ about $p(x^\prime)$ using the hypothesis on $u$. By [def-pc-fibre-product], $g(q(x^\prime))=u(p(x^\prime))\in u(V)\subset U$, so $q(x^\prime)\in g^{-1}(U)$. The latter is open by continuity of the scheme morphism $g$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] on $S^\prime$ to obtain an affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}C$ with $q(x^\prime)\in W\subset g^{-1}(U)$. Steps 1--3 produce an affine open $V^\prime$ containing $x^\prime$, with $q(V^\prime)\subset W$ and ind-etale coordinate map $C\to B\otimes_A C$. These are exactly the required local affine charts for $q$. Only $U,V,W$ have been assumed affine. Use Scheme.exists_affine_mem_range_and_range_subset to choose W, IsOpenImmersion.lift for W to U, and Spec.preimage for its coordinate map A to C. The actual new chart is Spec(B tensor_A C) mapped by pullbackSpecIso.inv followed by m; its point-membership follows from range_map and its second projection equation from pullbackSpecIso_inv_snd.

title: Affine ind-etale neighbourhood charts after arbitrary scheme base change
statement:
Let $u:T\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] such that for every point $x\in T$ there are affine open subschemes $V=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset T$, $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset S$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-open-immersion], with $x\in V$ and $u(V)\subset U$, for which the induced ring homomorphism $A\to B$ is ind-etale [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. For any scheme morphism $g:S'\to S$, put $T'=T\times_SS'$ and let $p:T'\to T$, $q:T'\to S'$ be its projections [def-pc-fibre-product]. For every point $x'\in T'$, every such pair $V,U$ about $p(x')$, and every affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}C\subset g^{-1}(U)$ containing $q(x')$, the open subscheme $V'=p^{-1}(V)\cap q^{-1}(W)$ contains $x'$ and has a canonical isomorphism
$$V'\cong V\times_UW\cong\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A C).$$
Under this isomorphism the restrictions of $p$ and $q$ are induced by $B\to B\otimes_A C$, $b\mapsto b\otimes1$, and $C\to B\otimes_A C$, $c\mapsto1\otimes c$, respectively. The latter ring homomorphism is ind-etale. In particular $q:T'\to S'$ satisfies the same local affine ind-etale chart condition at every point of $T'$. No finiteness, affineness, or separation condition on $g$, $S$, or $S'$ is imposed.
